before.title: 1.0 TSI leaking fuel injectors — emissions recall (Skoda code 24FQ)
before.description: Certain 1.0 TSI three-cylinder (EA211) Scala models built roughly 2018-2020 were recalled because the fuel injectors can have an excessively high leakage rate, letting fuel enter the combustion chamber unintentionally so the vehicle no longer meets legal emissions limits. The VW Group action covered ~9,192 vehicles across brands; the Skoda portion (Fabia, Kamiq, Karoq, Octavia, Rapid and Scala) used recall code 24FQ and affected 2,109 Skoda cars.
before.solution: Under recall 24FQ the dealer replaces the affected fuel injectors at no cost (approximately 2-3 hours of work). Owners should check their VIN against Skoda's recall lookup / the VW Group recall system to confirm whether the work has been carried out.

before.title: 1.5 TSI EVO (EA211) 'kangaroo' juddering and hesitation when pulling away cold
before.description: Scala models fitted with the 1.5 TSI EVO (EA211 evo, 110/150 PS), especially with the 6-speed manual, exhibit a well-documented low-speed 'kangaroo' effect: when pulling away in 1st gear or cruising at low revs in 2nd, the engine momentarily cuts throttle then surges, making the car hop and judder. It is most pronounced during the warm-up phase on cold mornings and is linked to the engine's cylinder-deactivation (ACT) and lean-burn fuelling strategy. This is a VW-Group-wide EA211 evo issue shared with the Octavia, Golf, T-Roc and SEAT/Audi equivalents, but it genuinely affects the Scala.
before.solution: VW Group issued ECU software updates (from February 2020 onward, SW series 04E906027M/N and later 04E906027AD/AF) that revise the cold-start fuelling and cylinder-transition mapping. Owners should have the dealer apply the latest engine ECU software under the kangaroo/hesitation TSB. Results are mixed: many report improvement, some report little change. Avoiding very low revs (short-shifting less, keeping revs above ~1,500 when cold) reduces it. No part replacement is required.

before.title: 1.6 TDI DPF clogging and oil dilution on short-journey use
before.description: Scala diesels (1.6 TDI, EA288) used mainly for short urban trips suffer DPF (diesel particulate filter) clogging because the exhaust rarely reaches the ~600 C needed for regeneration, so soot accumulates. Incomplete/interrupted regenerations also cause engine-oil dilution (diesel injected for regen washes into the sump), which can raise oil level and degrade lubrication. This is a VW-Group EA288 TDI pattern, the Scala included; Euro 6 cars can additionally see NOx-sensor and AdBlue/SCR injector crystallisation faults.
before.solution: Take the car for a sustained motorway drive (20+ minutes at higher revs) to allow a full active regeneration; persistent blockage needs a forced regen or DPF clean/replacement. For city-only use, shorten oil-change intervals to manage dilution. Address AdBlue/NOx warnings by replacing the faulty NOx sensor or clearing/replacing a crystallised AdBlue injector. Read fault codes to confirm whether it is DPF, NOx sensor, or SCR.
symptoms: Rising oil level / diesel smell in oil

before.title: 7-speed DSG (DQ200) jerky shifts and mechatronic failure
before.description: Scala models with the 7-speed dry-clutch DSG (DQ200/0AM) can develop jerky or hard shifts, hesitation/delay when accelerating from a standstill, and lurching during low-speed manoeuvres. The known DQ200 root cause is a mechatronic valve-body weakness: the aluminium housing wall where the high-pressure accumulator screws in is thin and can crack, losing the 60-70 bar control pressure, which initially causes jerky shifts and can progress to gear-selection faults and dashboard warnings. This is a VW-Group-wide DQ200 issue shared across Skoda/VW/SEAT/Audi but the Scala is among the affected models.
before.solution: Minor shift roughness sometimes improves with a DSG software/adaptation update and a mechatronic/transmission fluid service (DQ200 uses a separate mechatronic oil). Confirmed mechatronic faults require reconditioning or replacement of the mechatronic unit, ideally with the superseded/upgraded valve body that addresses the cracking. Clutch-pack replacement is the other common DQ200 repair. Read fault codes before deciding.

before.title: Air-conditioning weak/intermittent cooling and compressor/condenser faults
before.description: Owners report the Scala's air conditioning malfunctioning with uneven temperature distribution and reduced cooling, typically becoming noticeable after ~30,000 km. Specific causes include the AC compressor showing early wear (engaging then disengaging, giving intermittent cooling, then failing) and the front-mounted condenser being vulnerable to stone/road-debris damage and corrosion, which causes refrigerant loss — a pattern common across SEAT/Skoda VW-Group cars.
before.solution: Have the AC pressure and refrigerant checked; recharge if low and leak-test the condenser. A stone-damaged or corroded condenser is replaced (it sits low at the front). A failing compressor is replaced. Periodic refrigerant inspection (every ~50,000 km) and protecting/cleaning the condenser area help prevent failures.

before.title: Bolero/Amundsen infotainment freezing and random reboots
before.description: A very commonly reported Scala fault is the MIB-based infotainment head unit (Bolero and Amundsen systems) freezing, becoming unresponsive to touch, or spontaneously rebooting while driving. Owners report the screen going black and restarting as if power-cycling, sometimes getting stuck on the 'loading user profile' or Skoda logo screen at startup, and losing an active sat-nav route. Some report it within the first 10,000 km. Android Auto/Apple CarPlay connection dropouts with newer phones are also frequently mentioned.
before.solution: Dealers address this with infotainment software/firmware updates; a hard reset (long-press the power/volume knob ~10-20 seconds) often clears a frozen unit temporarily. Persistent cases require the MIB unit to be re-flashed or, in some cases, replaced under warranty. Check for the latest available infotainment update and for any campaign applicable to your VIN.
symptoms: Stuck on startup logo / loading profile

before.title: eCall / Online Connectivity Unit (OCU) emergency-call software fault — recall
before.description: Early Scala models (2019-2020 production) were subject to recalls covering the emergency-call (eCall) system. In one campaign the OCU (Online Connectivity Unit) software did not meet specification; in another an incorrect dataset was uploaded to the OCU. Either fault could impair the automatic emergency-call function, which is a safety concern because the car may not correctly contact emergency services after a crash. Logged with the UK DVSA and EU recall systems.
before.solution: Dealer reprograms/updates the OCU software (and in some cases reloads the correct dataset) free of charge under the eCall recall. Owners of 2019-2020 cars should verify by VIN that the eCall recall(s) have been completed.

before.title: Premature front brake pad and disc wear
before.description: Several Scala owners report faster-than-expected wear of the front brake pads and discs, leading to earlier-than-anticipated replacement and increased running costs. It is most often a maintenance/wear concern rather than a safety failure, but worn discs can cause vibration through the pedal/steering under braking.
before.solution: Inspect front pads and discs at service; replace pads (and discs if below minimum thickness or scored/warped) as a pair per axle. Using OE-quality friction material and ensuring caliper slide pins are free helps. Pad-wear sensor warnings should be acted on promptly.
